name: רְחוּם
summary: Four men of the return: a leader who came up with Zerubbabel (Ezr 2:2; Neh 12:3; Nehum in Neh 7:7); Rehum the commander (בְּעֵל־טְעֵם), who with Shimshai the scribe wrote against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes and stopped the work by force (Ezr 4:8–23, in the Aramaic); a Levite, son of Bani, who repaired the wall (Neh 3:17); and one of the heads who sealed the covenant (Neh 10:26). The form is a passive participle of the root, “shown compassion”, or an adjective beside רַחוּם “compassionate”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: Among those “who came with Zerubbabel … Bigvai, רְחוּם, Baanah”.
“רְחוּם the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king.”
They “made them cease by force and power”.
“After him the Levites repaired: Rehum son of Bani.”
רַחוּם “compassionate”, the adjective nearest in form.

note: Takes t.bz.ai (Hebrew, 8 tokens) and xt.ah.ad (the Aramaic of Ezr 4, BDB root רחומ). TIPNR's Rehum@Ezr.2.2 includes Neh 12:3 and the variants Harim and Nehum; its Rehum@Neh.10.25 is Neh 10:26 in the Hebrew numbering. Rehum of Ezr 4 was an official of the Persian province; his name is Aramaic in form and need not be Israelite. Whether רְחוּם is passive (“pitied”) or active (“compassionate”) cannot be decided from the form alone.
